title: Majority Fourier level and tail estimates
statement: Suppose that for each odd natural number $k$ a natural number $n(k)$ is specified, with $n(k)$ odd and $2k^2\le n(k)$. As $k$ tends to infinity through odd natural numbers, both the level-$k$ Fourier weight of majority on $n(k)$ variables, divided by $(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-3/2}$ and then decreased by $1$, and the Fourier weight above level $k$, divided by $(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-1/2}$ and then decreased by $1$, are each $O(1/k)$.
hypotheses_covered: A function $n$ assigning a natural number to each odd natural number $k$
